nodes.body:

### Electron Version

41.0.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Linux Mint 22.3 (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-110-generic)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Unknown

### Expected Behavior

In the `select-serial-port` IPC event, `portList[n].portName` should be the **full device node path**: `/dev/ttyUSB0` (or `/dev/ttyACM0`, `/dev/cu.usbserial-*` on macOS, etc.).

### Actual Behavior

`portName` contains the **device basename** (e.g. `ttyUSB0`) instead of the full device node path (`/dev/ttyUSB0`). 

`port.open()` succeeds in a minimal Fiddle (see Gist) despite the basename portName, so Electron correctly uses `portId` for the internal open. Still, this is a JS API inconsistency — code that reads `portName` to display or compare paths gets a misleading value.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/6233ad39e9927ab8195819c45f2912dc

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Add ability to stop heap profiling
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

`contentTracing.enableHeapProfiling()` allows the app developer to start the [heap profiling supervisor](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:components/heap_profiling/multi_process/supervisor.h;drc=83d6a18bb1a14348c1050905353aad9ba559d3be). Any traces recorded afterward will include heap dumps. However, after the trace is recorded, memory allocations will continue to be intercepted until the app is restarted.

It would be awesome to have a way to stop that.

Unfortunately, upstream doesn't support stopping heap profiling / the heap profiling supervisor yet (which is why this functionality wasn't included in #50826). In Chrome, once enabled, memory allocations will be recorded until the app is restarted.

@deepak1556 had great suggestions in https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50826#discussion_r3078384865:

> The heap profile supervisor process once started remains a process wide singleton, and will continue to intercept memory allocations from new and existing clients post the tracing. Could we get a change in upstream to make this start/stop on demand ? The other option would be to have our own supervisor that controls the lifetime of the heapprofilingservice but that would duplicate a lot of code with upstream, we can pursue that if addition of stop api is not possible in upstream.

### Proposed Solution

Two options:

1. Add a function `contentTracing.disableHeapProfiling()`
2. Refactor the API more broadly:
   - Remove `contentTracing.enableHeapProfiling()`
   - Add heap profiling options to the `contentTracing.startRecording()` `TraceConfig` instead, e.g.:
     ```js
     contentTracing.startRecording({
       heapProfiling: {
         mode: 'all',
         samplingRate: 100000,
         stackMode: 'native',
       }
     })
     ```
   - When heap profiling options are passed to `contentTracing.startRecording()`:
     - First start the heap profiling supervisor
     - Once the heap profiling supervisor has started, start the recording
   - When `contentTracing.stopRecording()` is called:
     - Stop the trace
     - Stop the heap profiling supervisor again

Option 2 has a cleaner API. (We marked `contentTracing.enableHeapProfiling()` as experimental to allow for exactly this kind of refactoring.)

Option 1 can work with:
- `--trace-startup=disabled-by-default-memory-infra --trace-startup-format=json --trace-startup-file=/path/to/trace.json` command line parameters to start profiling as early as possible
- [Chrome DevTools Protocol tracing](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Tracing/) (untested but I think it's likely to work)

This is a trade-off between having a nicer API or supporting more functionality.

### Alternatives Considered

See above. :)

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.2.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Home

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

I migrated Mailspring's notifications from custom toastXml over to the Electron Notification APIs and expected inline replies and actions to trigger `notification.on('reply')` and `notification.on('action')` but they do not.

### Actual Behavior

The action and reply events on Notification are silently dropped. The buttons and reply input render correctly in the toast, and click fires as expected, but action and reply never fire regardless of CLSID configuration. (I've added the new CLSID setter and verified a stable CLSID in the shortcut)

### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/codebytere/toast-actions-msix-sample/blob/main/src/main.ts, just without MSIX packaging

### Additional Information

In `windows_toast_notification.cc`, `ToastEventHandler::Invoke` handles the WinRT Activated event for all toast interactions. For structured arguments (action/reply), it returns early without dispatching:

```
bool structured = arguments_w.find(L"&tag=") != std::wstring::npos ||
                  arguments_w.find(L"type=action") != std::wstring::npos ||
                  arguments_w.find(L"type=reply") != std::wstring::npos;
if (structured)
  return S_OK;  // drops the event, waiting for COM callback
```

This design expects the COM `INotificationActivationCallback::Activate()` callback to handle action/reply. However, the toast XML uses activationType="foreground" for all action elements.

- MSIX-packaged apps: COM activation is declared in `AppxManifest.xml`. Windows invokes the COM activator for all activation types, so the early return in the WinRT handler works correctly — the COM callback fires and delivers the event.

- Unpackaged apps (Squirrel, NSIS, etc.): For `activationType="foreground"`, Windows fires only the WinRT in-process Activated event. No COM callback fires. The WinRT handler drops the event. Result: action and reply are permanently lost.

I have been deep in the weeds debugging this with Claude and I am no Windows API expert (I use a Mac!) but I have a context window full of Windows docs and Electron source :-) it suggests: 

- Option A (minimal): In `ToastEventHandler::Invoke`, call `HandleToastActivation()` directly for structured args received via the WinRT Activated event, rather than returning early. This handles the foreground activation path used by unpackaged apps and is a no-op for MSIX apps where the COM callback will also fire (one path would just win the race).

- Option B (correct Windows semantics): Change the generated toast XML to use `activationType="background"` for action/reply elements. This explicitly tells Windows to use the COM activation path, which works for both packaged and unpackaged apps (given `setToastActivatorCLSID` is called and the shortcut is correctly written). This also has the user-experience benefit of not foregrounding the app window for background actions like "Mark as Read".

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 26100

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

**NativeWindowViews::SetForwardMouseMessages** function unhooks the global mouse hook using **UnhookWindowsHookEx(mouse_hook_)** when the **forwarding_windows_** set becomes empty. It should verify the return value of **UnhookWindowsHookEx**

### Actual Behavior

If **UnhookWindowsHookEx** fails (returns FALSE), the existing hook remains active in the system. Because **mouse_hook_** is reset to **nullptr** regardless of success, subsequent calls to **SetForwardMouseMessages(true)** will evaluate **if (!mouse_hook_)** as true. This causes **SetWindowsHookEx** to be called again, installing an additional, duplicate mouse hook

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

nodes.title: npm/install.js: getPlatformPath ignores documented ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM env var
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0-nightly.20260413

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Reproduces on any host OS when installing an Electron binary for a different target OS via the postinstall script. Demonstrated here on Linux downloading a `darwin` / `win32` build.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

`ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM` is documented in [`docs/tutorial/installation.md`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/docs/tutorial/installation.md#customization) as the supported way to override the target platform for the Electron postinstall download. Setting it should make the postinstall script:

1. Download the zip for the requested platform.
2. Write `path.txt` containing the executable path **for that platform's build** (`electron.exe` for `win32`, `Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron` for `darwin`/`mas`, etc.).
3. Produce an `isInstalled()` result that reflects what is actually on disk, so subsequent installs don't re-download unnecessarily.

### Actual Behavior

`npm/install.js` resolves the target platform in two places and the two disagree when `ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM` is used.

The download path, added in #49981, honors the new env var:

```js
// npm/install.js, line ~20
const platform = process.env.ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM
  || process.env.npm_config_platform
  || process.platform;
```

But `getPlatformPath()`, which produces the executable path written to `path.txt` and compared during `isInstalled()`, was not updated:

```js
// npm/install.js, line ~98
function getPlatformPath() {
  const platform = process.env.npm_config_platform || os.platform();
  ...
}
```

Consequences on, for example, a Linux host running `ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM=darwin npm install electron`:

- The `darwin` zip is downloaded and extracted to `dist/` (correct).
- `path.txt` is written as `electron` (the Linux executable name), not `Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron`.
- On a subsequent install, `isInstalled()` runs `fs.existsSync(path.join(__dirname, 'dist', 'electron'))`, which does not exist in a `darwin` build, so the cache check fails and the zip is re-downloaded and re-extracted every time.
- Any tooling that reads `path.txt` to locate the Electron executable will read the wrong filename for the artifact that was actually extracted.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Minimal simulation of the branch taken by `getPlatformPath()`:

```js
// Simulating npm/install.js on a Linux host with ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM=darwin
process.env.ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM = 'darwin';

// Download resolution (after #49981): uses 'darwin' — downloads darwin zip
const downloadPlatform = process.env.ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM
  || process.env.npm_config_platform
  || process.platform;  // 'darwin'

// path.txt resolution (getPlatformPath): ignores ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM
const pathTxtPlatform = process.env.npm_config_platform || require('os').platform();
// => 'linux' on Linux, so path.txt is written as 'electron' alongside a darwin build.
```

The fix is a one-liner in `getPlatformPath()` that brings it in line with the download resolution:

```diff
 function getPlatformPath() {
-  const platform = process.env.npm_config_platform || os.platform();
+  const platform = process.env.ELECTRON_INSTALL_PLATFORM || process.env.npm_config_platform || os.platform();
```

I will open a PR implementing this.
